newsitem.title: FRANCE: De Dietrich plans share buy-back.
newsitem.headline: De Dietrich plans share buy-back.

text.p: French equipment maker De Dietrich said on Thursday it planned to buy back 18 percent of its shares in the market, with a view to cancelling the stock.

The board will call an extraordinary shareholders meeting to approve the plan, which also requires regulatory approval. It will offer 275 francs per share, totalling 367 million francs, it said in a statement.
"This operation aims to optimise use of the group's significant cash position by giving shareholders part of the capital available to the company," it said.
Trading in De Dietrich shares was suspended on Wednesday pending a company statement. The stock closed on Tuesday at 260 francs.

The group's activities include making heating equipment, equipment for the chemical and pharmaceutical industries, railway and other mechanical equipment, the manufacture and installation of railway track and forestry related activities.
